sentences.text:
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973(Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing No. 1094/2015 registered at Police Station Amar Colony, New Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Amol Sinha, learned ASC (Crl.) accepts notice on behalf of the State.
5. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. R.D. Singh and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Chanchal, Police Station Amar Colony, New Delhi.

sentences.text: Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 26.06.2010.
A female child was born out of the said wedlock.
It is stated that due to temperamental differences arose between the parties, they started living separately from each other since 02.06.2015.

On the basis of complaint filed by respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing No.
1094/2015 at Police Station Amar Colony, New Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 was registered against petitioners.

entities.text: Police Station Amar Colony, New Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 vide decree sheet dated 18.01.2023 by way of mutual consent dissolved their marriage.

During the pendency of the present FIR, with the intervention of family members and respectable person of the society, both the parties had amicably settled their disputes vide Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) dated 05.10.2022.
7.

On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide MoU dated 05.10.2022 and learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that affidavit showing the protection of interest of minor child as per the judgment titled as Ganesh vs. Sudhirkumar Shrivastava, (2020) 20 SCC 787 passed by the Honble Supreme Court has been filed along with petition.
8.

It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner.

9. The petitioner had paid a sum of Rs. 20,00,000/- in three instalments in the following manner:
a. First instalment of Rs.5,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording statements in the first motion petition.
b. Second instalment of Rs.5,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording statements in the second motion petition.

c.
Third/Final instalment of Rs.10,00,000/- to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Honble High Court at New Delhi.

10. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. Rs.10,00,000/- today, i.e., 15.02.2023 by way of DD bearing No. 607555 for a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- drawn on State Bank of India, New Delhi and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

11. In view of the above fact that the parties have amicably resolved their differences of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

12. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 1094/2015 registered at Police Station Amar Colony, New Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings Marut Prasad & Ors vs The State Govt.
